section_1.title: The Familiar Intuition: Real Convergence
section_1.content: Briefly review the standard Euclidean metric where a series converges if its tail approaches zero. Use a visual 'number line' where terms get physically smaller in distance.
section_1.example: A squirrel moving halfway to a nut at each step: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... leads to the nut at position 1.

section_2.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
section_2.content: Define the 2-adic norm: |x|_2 = 1/2^k, where k is the highest power of 2 dividing x. Explain that in this world, numbers are 'close' if their difference is divisible by a high power of 2. Visual: A fractal-like tree structure (the 2-adic tree) showing branching levels.
section_2.example: Compare 4 and 12: |4-12|_2 = | -8 |_2 = 1/8. They are 'closer' than 1 and 2, where |1-2|_2 = 1.

section_3.title: Paradoxical Convergence
section_3.content: Demonstrate the core property: a series converges if and only if its terms approach 0 in the 2-adic sense. Show that powers of 2 (2, 4, 8, 16...) shrink toward zero.
section_3.example: Visual animation of a '2-adic clock' where the hands jump by powers of 2; as the exponent grows, the position converges to the 'center' (zero).

section_4.title: The Grand Finale: Summing to Infinity
section_4.content: Reveal the counter-intuitive result: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... = -1 in the 2-adic metric. Connect this back to the geometric series formula 1/(1-r) where r=2.
section_4.example: A magical '2-adic calculator' that adds powers of 2. As we add more terms, the binary representation fills up with 1s, which visually represents -1 in two's complement arithmetic.

section_5.title: Summary and Perspective
section_5.content: Recap that 'convergence' depends on the choice of metric. Reiterate that while Euclidean distance measures 'size', the 2-adic metric measures 'divisibility'.
section_5.example: A map of the same mathematical landscape viewed through two different lenses: one measures physical distance, the other measures '2-adic' closeness.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
